messages:
Jamal: Quick heads-up — starting a short thread for this month's recurring-incident themes review. Pulled last 90 days, top 5 recurring causes attached. Please skim and call out owners for remediation items.

Emily: sending the doc now — https://redwood.docs/incident-patterns/mar-2026 (TL;DR: autoscale flapping, KV cache invalidation, quantized OOMs, rollout mismatch, and third-party auth rate limits)

Alex: thanks. I can take ownership of KV cache invalidation fixes. Proposed timeline: investigation + small patch by 3/20, canary for two weeks, then full rollout.

Maya: tagging infra — @Chris, can infra help with autoscale tuning and a more conservative drain policy? That'll likely reduce the flapping noise.

Chris: yep. I can do an autoscale policy audit. Will need 3 days to collect metrics. ETA 3/18. Also suggest adding a simple hysteresis: min-stable-window=120s.

Emily: noted — Alex + Chris to collaborate on cache + autoscale. Can you both own the cross-team action item? I'll add to the postmortem tracker.

Alex: yes, I'll own cross-team. Adding action item: "Investigate KV cache invalidation during scale events" — owner: Alex, collaborator: Chris — due 2026-03-22.

Maya: on quantized OOMs — we saw transient OOMs when load spikes hit long context requests. Ops suggests limiting max-concurrency per instance and enabling swap-buffering for quantized kernels. @Jamal any objections?

Jamal: no objections. We should avoid config that changes customer-visible latency. Proposed: safe defaults in prod + feature flag for aggressive memory optimizations.

Chris: agree. I'll prepare a safe default and a rollout plan. Owner: Chris, due 2026-03-25.

Emily: external auth rate limit — appears to be 3rd-party throttling during high fan-out jobs. Short-term mitigation: backoff + jitter; longer-term: token caching and retry budget. @Product-ops can weigh in?

Jamal: product-ops okayed token caching last week. Emily, can you coordinate with Solutions to scope change?

Emily: will do. Adding action: "Implement token caching + retry budget for auth calls" — owner: Emily, due 2026-04-05.

Alex: one more theme — rollout mismatch: model v2 was deployed to 30% but some routes still hit v1 leading to desynced caches. Suggest we add a rollout fencing check in the router that enforces consistent model variant per session.

Maya: agree. That sounds like a router change. Owner: Maya, due 2026-04-01. Also propose a post-rollout smoke test that verifies kv-cache hits and latency SLOs.

SRE Bot: Reminder — please add action items to /incident-tracker. Use format: "Title | Owner | Due | Notes".

Emily: done. I added the five items and linked the analytics query used for patterns.

Jamal: good. Two procedural asks: 1) can we get monthly trendline charts in the ops dashboard (top-5 causes) so we don't re-run ad-hoc queries? 2) rotate remediation on-call so action owners don't become single points of failure.

Chris: for (1) I can wire the queries into the dashboard. For (2) agree — propose a 3-person rotation: Alex, Maya, Chris as primary responders for pattern remediation.

Alex: works for me. Can someone schedule a 30-min sync to align owners and dependencies?

Maya: I'll create a calendar invite for 3/16 10:00-10:30 PT and include the checklist: data sources, runbook updates, rollout plan per item, and required infra changes.

OpsBot: /remind #incidents "Monthly recurring-incident review: follow up on open action items" on 2026-04-15 09:00

Jamal: thanks. Last bit — let's add a short blurb to the next all-hands about the top remediation areas and ask teams to block small maintenance windows to implement fixes. Keeps visibility high. :eyes:

Emily: agreed. I'll draft a 3-bullet note for all-hands.

Chris: quick question — are we capturing customer-impacted incidents vs internal-only flaps separately in the tracker? We should prioritize customer-impacting ones.

Alex: yes, tracker has a severity flag. I'll mark the KV cache item as high-priority since it caused degraded responses for some tenants.

Emily: wrapping up: owners and due dates: Alex (KV cache) 2026-03-22, Chris (autoscale + mem defaults) 2026-03-25, Maya (router rollout fence) 2026-04-01, Emily (auth token caching) 2026-04-05, Chris (dashboard trendlines) 2026-03-20. If anyone needs extensions ping here.

Jamal: perfect. Thanks all. If no objections I'll close this thread and track progress in the incident tracker.

Maya: no objections.

Alex: all good from me.

SRE Bot: Action items created: 5. Next reminder scheduled for 2026-04-15.
